nodes.label: Bishnoi Community
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: In Rajasthan, community that protects wildlife and khejri trees. 363 Bishnois sacrificed their lives in 1731 to protect khejri trees from Jodhpur's Maharaja. Led to Chipko-like conservation ethos.

nodes.label: Inland Waterways
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Cheapest transport mode. National Waterway 1: Ganga (Allahabad-Haldia, 1620 km). NW 2: Brahmaputra (Sadiya-Dhubri, 891 km). NW 3: W Coast Canal (Kollam-Kottapuram, 205 km). NW 4: K-G basins.

nodes.label: HBJ Pipeline
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Hazira-Bijaipur-Jagdishpur pipeline carrying natural gas from Gujarat to UP. 1700 km long. Connects gas fields to fertiliser and power plants in north India.

nodes.label: Shola Forests
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Unique tropical montane forests (stunted evergreen) found in the valleys and sheltered slopes of the Western Ghats above 1,500m, interspersed with grasslands on hill tops. Found in Nilgiris, Anaimalai, and Palani Hills. Extremely fragile ecosystem with high endemism. Threatened by eucalyptus and wattle plantations.

nodes.label: Atmosphere
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Gaseous layer surrounding earth extending up to 1600 km. Five layers: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere, exosphere. 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 1% other gases.

nodes.label: Himalayan Mountain Ranges
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Three parallel ranges: Himadri (Great Himalaya, northernmost, highest peaks), Himachal (Middle Himalaya, popular hill stations), Shiwalik (southernmost range). Him+alaya means abode of snow.

nodes.label: Natural Vegetation
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Grasses, shrubs and trees growing without human interference. Five types in India: tropical evergreen, tropical deciduous, thorny bushes, mountain vegetation, mangroves. Dependent on climatic conditions especially rainfall.

nodes.label: Rice
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Major food crop of the world, staple of tropical/subtropical regions. Needs high temperature, humidity, rainfall and alluvial clayey soil. China leads production followed by India. 2-3 crops per year in favourable conditions.

nodes.label: Tropical Evergreen Forests (India)
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Areas with 200cm+ rainfall. Dense canopy, no definite leaf-shedding time. Trees: ebony, mahogany, rosewood, cinchona, rubber. Found: Western Ghats, NE hills, Andaman-Nicobar. Animals: elephant, monkey, lemur, deer.

nodes.label: Tropical Deciduous Forests (India)
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Most widespread in India. 70-200cm rainfall. Moist deciduous (100-200cm): teak, sal, shisham, sandalwood; in NE, Western Ghats foothills, Jharkhand. Dry deciduous (70-100cm): teak, sal, peepal, neem; in peninsular plateau.

nodes.label: Tropical Thorn Forests
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Below 70cm rainfall. NW India: Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, UP. Acacias, palms, euphorbias, cacti. Trees scattered with long roots, thick bark, waxy leaves. Animals: rats, mice, rabbits, fox, wild ass, camels.

nodes.label: Mangrove Forests (India)
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Tidal/coastal forests in river deltas. Dense, salt-tolerant. Sundarbans largest mangrove forest (Royal Bengal Tiger). Bhitarkanika (Odisha), Pichavaram (TN). Trees: sundari, keora, agar. Roots submerged in water.
